findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Hoover sign, collapsing weakness and distractible tremor on the right; sensory splitting supportive only
action_criteria.label: Examine for positive functional signs
action_criteria.rationale: The diagnosis is made at the bedside: a positive Hoover sign, collapsing weakness and a distractible tremor are signs of clinical incompatibility (DSM-5 criterion B; Daum 2014).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No T2/FLAIR lesion or restricted diffusion to account for the right leg weakness
action_criteria.label: Non-contrast brain MRI, once
action_criteria.rationale: Acute right leg weakness with a remitting episode in the same limb two years ago raises demyelination or a structural lesion; one non-contrast MRI with DWI answers that question, and gadolinium adds nothing without a known demyelinating disease (Espay 2018).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm with normal conduction and QT interval
action_criteria.label: 12-lead ECG
action_criteria.rationale: Episodes of apparent unresponsiveness: NICE advises a 12-lead ECG after transient loss of consciousness (CG109) and after a suspected seizure (NG217). The event semiology already favours functional seizures, so it does not contribute to the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Habitual events recorded on video with no EEG change and a normal interictal record
action_criteria.label: Video-EEG to capture a habitual event
action_criteria.rationale: The events have one feature that favours epileptic seizures (eyes open with upward gaze), so the semiology is less conclusive than usual; a habitual event recorded on video-EEG without ictal change reaches the ILAE documented level and lets co-occurring epilepsy be assessed (LaFrance 2013; AAN 2025). Without the recording, the positive signs and the semiology of witnessed events support the diagnosis at a lower ILAE level of certainty (LaFrance 2013).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction between sertraline and dicyclomine that alters the plan
action_criteria.label: Review the medication list
action_criteria.rationale: Sertraline and PRN dicyclomine carry no interaction that changes management and no benzodiazepine or antiseizure drug is prescribed; the review is defensible but not needed for the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Quantifies mood, anxiety and symptom burden to guide therapy; does not make the diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological assessment of the comorbidity
action_criteria.rationale: Generalized anxiety disorder is a treatment target; a battery can quantify it but does not make the diagnosis and is not needed before treatment (Espay 2018).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on positive signs and treatment trials in FND
action_criteria.label: Search the literature on FND diagnosis and treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; the diagnosis and the plan rest on this patient's examination and recorded data, not on a search.

prohibited_recommendations: Order further investigations once the positive diagnosis is established, without a new specific clinical question (repeat MRI, CT, lumbar puncture, EMG or nerve conduction studies, evoked potentials, PET).
Tell the patient the symptoms are imagined, feigned, 'all in your head', or that nothing is wrong.
Perform invasive testing without a specific indication (lumbar puncture, nerve or muscle biopsy, catheter angiography).
Start or escalate antiseizure medication for the functional seizures.
Give benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional seizure.
Give gadolinium contrast without a specific indication.
required_recommendations: Make a positive diagnosis of functional neurological disorder (mixed: functional seizures and functional right leg weakness) based on the Hoover sign, collapsing weakness and distractible tremor and the semiology of the habitual events, confirmed on video-EEG where recorded, and not by exclusion of other disease.

Explain the diagnosis to the patient, and with consent to the family, as a common and genuine disorder of nervous system functioning that can improve, show the positive signs, and give written information.
Refer for physiotherapy with expertise in functional motor disorder (motor retraining, Nielsen 2015 consensus).
Refer for psychological therapy by a clinician experienced in FND (CBT-informed) and treat the comorbid anxiety.

Give the patient, family and ward a written plan for typical events: keep safe, do not restrain, wait for the event to end, and do not give emergency benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional seizure.

avoided_actions.rationale: No murmur, embolic or structural cardiac question in a 28-year-old with functional weakness and events.
The events are not syncopal: 2-3 minutes of bilateral shaking without pallor, not a brief collapse; rhythm monitoring answers no question here.
Three days into the weakness, with no thrombolysis question, a head CT adds radiation and answers nothing the single MRI does not.
No fever, meningism or encephalopathy; a lumbar puncture is invasive and answers no question once positive signs are documented.
PET has no role in functional weakness or functional seizures.
Reflexes are normal and the weakness has positive functional signs; nerve conduction studies and EMG answer no question and a normal study reinforces the search for an organic cause.
Sensory loss splitting the midline at the groin is not a somatosensory pathway question; evoked potentials add nothing.

accepted: Functional neurological disorder — functional limb weakness (right leg) and PNES (psychogenic non-epileptic seizures)

differential.key_features: Eyes open during the events favour epileptic seizures, but she followed a command during bilateral shaking and recovered at once. A habitual event recorded on video-EEG without ictal change; co-occurring epilepsy remains possible in about one in five patients with functional seizures.

A remitting episode of right leg weakness two years ago raises demyelination, but the Hoover sign and collapsing weakness with normal reflexes and flexor plantars are incompatible with a central lesion, and the non-contrast MRI shows no white matter lesion.

differential.diagnosis: Ischemic stroke or other structural brain lesion
differential.key_features: Weakness developed over 3 days rather than abruptly; positive functional signs, normal reflexes and a normal MRI without restricted diffusion or mass argue against it.

key_clinical_evidence: Positive signs of functional weakness and tremor: right Hoover sign, collapsing weakness of the right leg and a right hand tremor that stops with serial 7s; midline-splitting sensory loss and normal walking when unobserved are supportive only.

Event semiology: bilateral arm shaking for 2-3 minutes with no incontinence, no postictal confusion and immediate recovery; the open eyes are an atypical feature, so the semiology alone does not settle the events.
Video-EEG recorded one habitual event, confirmed as typical by the roommate, with no EEG change and responsiveness to command during the shaking; the interictal record is normal.
A single non-contrast brain MRI, indicated by the prior remitting right leg episode, shows no white matter lesion or other structural cause.
The recent divorce and custody dispute and her generalized anxiety are supportive context and a treatment target; a stressor is neither required nor sufficient for the diagnosis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Psychiatric comorbidity neither establishes nor refutes FND; the diagnosis rests on the positive signs and the event semiology, and the anxiety is a treatment target.
red_herrings.data_point: Generalized anxiety disorder treated with sertraline
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchoring on a 'psychosomatic' label without eliciting positive signs, or dismissing the symptoms as anxiety

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A stressor is supportive context only; it is neither required nor sufficient for the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Divorce finalized 3 weeks ago with a custody dispute
red_herrings.intended_effect: Concluding that stress 'caused' the symptoms and skipping the examination and the event recording

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Open eyes are more frequent in epileptic seizures, but no single semiological feature is diagnostic; the habitual event recorded without ictal EEG change decides.
red_herrings.data_point: Eyes open and rolled back during the episodes
red_herrings.intended_effect: Treating the events as epileptic and starting antiseizure medication

sequence_constraints.reason: The examination comes first: its positive signs decide whether imaging has a specific question to answer (Espay 2018).

findings.result: Right hip extension absent on direct testing, full strength during contralateral left hip flexion against resistance.
Right leg strength collapses suddenly after a brief normal effort on each tested movement.
Right hand tremor stops while she performs serial 7s and returns when the task ends.
Right leg sensory loss splitting the midline at the groin; normal walking in the hallway when unaware of being observed; not counted as rule-in signs.
Reflexes 2+ and symmetric; plantar responses flexor.

clinical_assessment.impression: Positive signs of functional weakness and tremor: Hoover sign, collapsing weakness of the right leg and distractible right hand tremor. The pattern is inconsistent with a structural lesion. No event was observed during the examination.

general.proposed: Sertraline 50 mg once daily; Dicyclomine 10 mg as needed up to 3 times daily
general.summary: No clinically significant interactions among the current medicines.
warnings: Dicyclomine: anticholinergic effects (dizziness, blurred vision, drowsiness) at higher or repeated doses.

artifacts.description: Myogenic artifact during the event, without underlying rhythmic evolution

background.description: Well-organized 10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, reactive to eye opening. Normal sleep architecture with vertex waves and spindles.
background.recording: 48-hour inpatient video-EEG, wake and sleep, 10-20 electrode placement

findings.morphology: Day 1, 15:42, duration 2 min 35 s: bilateral asynchronous arm shaking of waxing and waning amplitude, eyes open with upward gaze, no speech; she squeezed the technologist's hand on command midway through the event and returned to baseline immediately afterwards. The roommate confirmed on video review that the event was typical. Posterior dominant rhythm visible between bursts of muscle artifact throughout; no evolving rhythmic activity, no postictal slowing or attenuation.

eeg.impression: This is a NORMAL video-EEG. One habitual event was recorded (bilateral asynchronous arm shaking with eyes open, lasting 2 min 35 s) without ictal EEG change before, during or after the event; the posterior dominant rhythm persisted during the event. No interictal epileptiform discharges. No electrographic seizures.

results.finding: Diagnosis of functional neurological disorder rests on positive clinical features such as the Hoover sign, tremor entrainment and functional seizure semiology, not on the exclusion of other disease; treatment combines explanation, physiotherapy and psychological therapy.
results.source: Espay AJ et al. JAMA Neurol 2018;75:1132-1141

results.finding: Motor signs such as the Hoover sign, hip abductor sign, drift without pronation and dragging gait have high specificity; sensory signs such as midline splitting have low specificity.
results.source: Daum C et al. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2014;85:180-190

results.finding: Defines levels of certainty for psychogenic nonepileptic seizures; the documented level requires a typical event recorded on video-EEG without ictal EEG change.
results.source: LaFrance WC Jr et al. Epilepsia 2013;54:2005-2018

results.finding: For functional seizures: assess for co-occurring epilepsy and psychiatric disorders, taper antiseizure medication without another indication, avoid benzodiazepines, and offer psychological therapy, which is possibly effective.
CBT added to standardised medical care did not reduce dissociative seizure frequency at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured CBT.
results.source: Goldstein LH et al. Lancet Psychiatry 2020;7:491-505

results.finding: Specialist physiotherapy for functional motor disorder was not superior to community neurological physiotherapy on physical function at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured it.
results.source: Nielsen G et al. Lancet Neurol 2024;23:675-686

results.finding: About 4% of patients diagnosed with conversion symptoms since 1970 later received another diagnosis.

functional neurological disorder diagnos.summary: Guideline and trial evidence supports a positive clinical diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, video-EEG confirmation of functional seizures, tapering of unneeded antiseizure drugs and benzodiazepines, and physiotherapy and psychological treatment whose trial effects on primary outcomes were modest.

additional_observations: Technique: sagittal T1, axial T2, axial and sagittal FLAIR, DWI with ADC, SWI; no contrast administered
No T2/FLAIR white matter lesion; no periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial or callosal lesion
mri.impression: Normal non-contrast brain MRI. No white matter lesion, restricted diffusion, mass or hemorrhage.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Clear positive signs of functional right leg weakness and tremor, but the events include an atypical feature (eyes open), so a video-EEG capture adds most here; one non-contrast MRI answers the demyelination question raised by the prior remitting episode.
metadata.notes: Straightforward FND with PNES and functional right leg weakness. The Hoover sign is diagnostic of the weakness; a video-EEG capture confirms the events.
metadata.revision_reason: October 2026 review round: criteria rebuilt to the pack tiers (exam required, MRI recommended), non-contrast MRI, canonical literature and medication outputs, case-specific differential, evidence and assessment. Close-out 24 Oct 2026: video-EEG optional and red-flag tests recommended, per the July 2026 agreement with the physicians that the examination is the only required diagnostic act.

patient.chief_complaint: Right leg weakness over 3 days and two episodes of unresponsiveness

medications.frequency: as needed up to 3 times daily

social_history.recent_stressor: Divorce finalized 3 weeks ago after contentious 18-month separation; custody dispute for 4-year-old daughter

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. L is a 28-year-old elementary school teacher who was brought to the emergency department by ambulance after two witnessed episodes of unresponsiveness at home this morning. The episodes were described by her roommate as lasting 2-3 minutes with bilateral arm shaking, eyes open and rolled back, no post-ictal confusion, and immediate return to baseline after each episode. She also reports complete right leg weakness developing over the past 3 days, making it impossible for her to walk. She has no prior history of seizures or epilepsy. She is being admitted for monitoring and workup. On further history, she reports that her divorce was finalized 3 weeks ago following a contentious 18-month separation, with ongoing custody dispute for her 4-year-old daughter. She denies any head trauma, fever, or recent illness. She notes a similar episode of weakness affecting the right leg approximately 2 years ago, which her previous doctor attributed to stress and which resolved over several weeks without treatment. She denies headache, vision changes, or speech difficulty. She is currently prescribed sertraline for anxiety, which was started 6 months ago. She is not on any anticonvulsants. She denies illicit drug use. Collateral from roommate confirms no incontinence during episodes and rapid complete recovery.

neurological_exam.additional: Collapsing (give-way) weakness of the right leg on testing. Mild right hand tremor that stops while she performs serial 7s.
neurological_exam.coordination: Normal bilateral upper extremities. Unable to assess right leg due to apparent weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No facial asymmetry. EOMI intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to weight-bear on right leg in room; observed walking normally in hallway when unaware of being observed.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Distressed and tearful. Cooperative but anxious.
neurological_exam.motor: Right leg 0/5 on formal testing. Hoover sign positive: right hip extension is absent on direct testing but returns to full strength, felt under the right heel, during contralateral left hip flexion against resistance. Left leg 5/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Normal 2+ symmetric throughout. No Babinski. No Hoffman.
neurological_exam.sensory: Right leg sensory loss splitting the midline exactly at the groin crease.
